SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Printing Materials for printing (soil, ash, charcoal dust, chalk dust, paper, feathers, grass), part of MYSELF THEME: MYSELF Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Lear in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we make hand prints? 2. How do we make hand prints?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify materials used in joining dots,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Printing Materials for printing (soil, ash, charcoal dust, chalk dust, paper, feathers, grass) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. join dots to make pictures of clothes worn by family

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Printing Materials for printing (soil, ash, charcoal dust, chalk dust, paper, feathers, grass) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify materials used in joining dots,

   Printing Materials for printing (soil, ash, charcoal dust, chalk dust, paper, feathers, grass) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. join dots to make pictures of clothes worn by family

   Printing Materials for printing (soil, ash, charcoal dust, chalk dust, paper, feathers, grass) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Sing familiar song about body parts. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech, hum or mime familiar songs.

2. Collect materials for making hand and foot printing. Safety precautions for all the learners should be observed with extra caution taken for learners with 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Sing familiar song about body parts. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech, hum or mime familiar songs.
2. Collect materials for making hand and foot printing. Safety precautions for all the learners should be observed with extra caution taken for learners with 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Printing Materials for printing (soil, ash, charcoal dust, chalk dust, paper, feathers, grass) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: Learner displays confidence in talking about clothes worn by family members.

● Communication and collaboration: Learner speaks about clothes worn by family members while collaborating with others.

Values:
● Love: Learner portrays a caring attitude by sharing materials with peers as they carry out their work.

● Responsibility: Learner distributes materials amongst themselves, store their works well and clear working areas.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Learners develop life skills of self-awareness while appreciating their own hand or foot prints.

Link to other learning areas:

Learners keep the working environment clean in environmental activities.
